name: Password Guessing
description: Adversaries with no prior knowledge of valid credentials may guess them through brute force or password spraying against authentication services such as SSH, RDP, web portals, and database logins. High-volume guessing produces distinctive failure patterns, either many attempts against one account or one password tried against many accounts.
mitigations: Enforce account lockout and exponential backoff after repeated failures
Deploy multi-factor authentication on all remote access points
Alert on authentication failure spikes grouped by source IP, account, and target
Apply rate limiting and CAPTCHA on internet-facing login forms

name: Network Service Discovery
description: Adversaries scan networks to discover open ports, running services, and live hosts, typically as reconnaissance before exploitation. Scanning may be performed with tools such as nmap and masscan or with native network utilities, and often precedes targeted exploitation of a discovered service.
mitigations: Segment the network and restrict cross-zone scanning paths
Tune IDS/IPS signatures for SYN sweeps and scanning patterns
Disable or firewall unnecessary services and ports
Baseline host-to-host traffic and alert on new connection patterns

name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
description: Adversaries exfiltrate data over an existing command-and-control channel instead of opening a separate connection, blending theft with routine C2 traffic to evade detection. Large or sustained outbound transfers to previously unseen destinations are a key indicator.
mitigations: Deploy DLP controls on egress points
Baseline outbound volume per host and alert on significant deviation
Restrict outbound traffic to approved destinations and ports via proxy
Inspect TLS traffic where feasible to identify tunneling anomalies

name: PowerShell
description: Adversaries abuse PowerShell to execute commands, download payloads, and run encoded or obfuscated scripts (for example via the -enc flag). PowerShell is a common vector for fileless attacks and post-exploitation activity on Windows hosts, especially on servers where interactive logins are unexpected.
mitigations: Enable PowerShell script block and transcript logging
Apply constrained language mode and application control policies
Alert on encoded-command and hidden-window flags on servers
Restrict interactive PowerShell access for service and application accounts

name: Valid Accounts
tactic: Defense Evasion, Persistence, Privilege Escalation, Initial Access
description: Adversaries use compromised, default, or legitimately obtained credentials such as admin, service, and backup accounts to appear as authorized users, bypassing access controls and defeating credential-based defenses. Logins from unfamiliar sources or at unusual times for otherwise valid accounts are primary indicators.
mitigations: Deploy multi-factor authentication for all privileged and remote access
Monitor for anomalous account usage: new source IPs, odd hours, impossible travel
Rotate and inventory service, backup, and default account credentials
Disable dormant accounts and enforce least-privilege role design

name: Create Account
description: Adversaries create new local or domain accounts to maintain access after password resets or account cleanup. Accounts may be hidden using registry tricks or naming that mimics legitimate service accounts, and are often added directly to privileged groups.
mitigations: Alert on account creation events, especially outside business hours
Audit for hidden accounts (registry SpecialAccounts) and unexpected group additions
Restrict who can create local accounts on servers
Run periodic account attestation reviews against HR records

name: Web Protocols
description: Adversaries use common web protocols such as HTTP and HTTPS for command-and-control traffic to blend in with normal browsing and API activity. Techniques include domain fronting, fast-flux domains, and beaconing on regular intervals to attacker-controlled endpoints.
mitigations: Force web egress through inspecting proxies with allow-lists
Monitor DNS logs for newly registered and low-reputation domains
Detect periodic beaconing patterns in outbound traffic
Block direct-to-internet server traffic where architecturally possible

name: OS Credential Dumping
description: Adversaries extract credentials from the operating system and software, including LSASS process memory, the SAM/SYSTEM/SECURITY registry hives, the NTDS.dit domain database, Kerberos tickets, and passwords stored in browsers. Credential dumping frequently follows initial access and enables lateral movement.
mitigations: Enable Credential Guard and LSASS protection (RunAsPPL)
Deploy EDR detections for common dumping tools and abnormal LSASS access
Use privileged access workstations and tiered administration
Harden service accounts with credential guard policies

name: Remote Services: SSH
description: Adversaries use SSH with stolen keys or credentials to move laterally between hosts, often via jump hosts, establishing encrypted sessions that resemble routine administration. Failed SSH attempts followed by a first-time successful login are a classic lateral movement signature.
mitigations: Use bastion hosts with full session logging and recording
Restrict SSH source ranges and disable password authentication
Rotate and inventory authorized SSH keys
Alert on SSH brute-force patterns and new user-host pairs

name: Account Manipulation
description: Adversaries modify existing accounts to maintain and elevate access, including adding accounts to privileged groups, registering new SSH keys, changing credentials, and configuring delegation or service principals. These changes survive password resets of the originally compromised account.
mitigations: Alert on modifications to privileged group membership
Monitor directory service events for unusual attribute and key changes
Require change approval workflows for privileged group membership
Regularly audit delegation, SPN, and authorized key configurations

name: Encrypted Channel
description: Adversaries encrypt command-and-control traffic using symmetric or asymmetric cryptography and sometimes custom protocols to evade network inspection. Unexpected certificate changes, self-signed certificates on services, and unusual cipher or protocol usage often accompany encrypted C2 setup.
mitigations: Inspect TLS at the proxy and validate certificate chains
Alert on unauthorized certificate replacement on servers
Block non-standard encrypted protocols on egress traffic
Detect unusual cipher suites and TLS fingerprints

name: Exfiltration to Cloud Storage
description: Adversaries transfer stolen data to legitimate cloud storage services such as object storage, file-sync platforms, and personal cloud drives, abusing trusted services and valid tokens to bypass traditional egress controls. Uploads are often large, sustained, and from service accounts or endpoints that rarely use those services.
mitigations: Apply DLP inspection to uploads toward cloud storage services
Restrict approved storage services and block personal cloud destinations
Monitor and scope cloud API tokens and access keys
Baseline host upload volumes and alert on large deviations
